question:
(i) State de Broglie relation for a moving particle and explain its physical meaning.
(ii) Use de Broglie’s idea to obtain Bohr’s angular momentum quantisation condition for an electron in a stable circular orbit.

options.A:
(i) $\lambda=hp$, so wavelength increases with momentum.
(ii) $2\pi r=\lambda/n$, giving $mvr=\dfrac{h}{2\pi n}$.
options.B:
(i) de Broglie relation applies only to photons, not electrons.
(ii) Bohr quantisation cannot be obtained from matter waves.
options.C:
(i) de Broglie relation is $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{p}=\dfrac{h}{mv}$; it means moving particles can show wave behaviour.
(ii) Stable circular orbits require $2\pi r=n\lambda$. With $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{mv}$, this gives $mvr=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.
options.D:
(i) $p=h\lambda$, so wavelength increases with momentum.
(ii) The condition is $mvr=nh$.
